blocks.html:
What to know

  • Fed state: insulin dominates. Insulin promotes glucose uptake, glycogen synthesis, fat storage, and protein synthesis.
  • Fasting state: glucagon dominates. Glucagon promotes glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and ketogenesis; insulin falls.
  • Basal metabolic rate is the largest component of energy use. It depends on body size, composition, age, sex, and thyroid status; activity adds variable cost.
  • Macronutrients have different roles. Protein supplies amino acids; carbohydrate supplies glucose and fiber; fat supplies essential fatty acids and fat-soluble vitamins.
  • Micronutrients are cofactors and regulators. Vitamins and minerals support enzymes and processes; deficiencies produce specific clinical patterns (for example iron-deficiency anemia, vitamin D deficiency).

Check

check.question: Which hormone rises during fasting and stimulates liver glucose release?
check.explanation: Glucagon rises when blood glucose falls and drives glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in the liver.
